title: Compensability Positions and the Form 63 Contest Period — Workers' Compensation Referral
content:
# Compensability positions and the Form 63 contest period

Compensability on a Workers' Compensation Referral follows the carrier's filed position with the North Carolina Industrial Commission:

| Filed position | Meaning on the referral |
|---|---|
| Form 60 — accepted | the carrier has accepted the claim |
| Form 63 — paid without prejudice | the carrier pays while keeping its right to deny |
| Form 61 — denied | the carrier has denied the claim |
| Pending | the carrier has not yet taken a position |
| Not applicable | carried by employer direct programs |

## The Form 63 contest period

A claim paid without prejudice is recorded as accepted no earlier than the program's Form 63 contest period, in calendar days, after the Form 63 date on file, and only when the carrier has not denied it by then. Days are counted as calendar days from the Form 63 date, the Form 63 date itself being day zero.

- **The clock starts** on the Form 63 date shown on the referral record.
- **Counting** is in calendar days, with the Form 63 date as day zero.
- **Direction and boundary** — acceptance may be recorded on the day the count reaches the contest period or on any later day; the day the count equals the contest period qualifies.
- **The second condition** — the carrier has not denied the claim by then.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, for a program whose contest period is 90 days)

| Day of the count | Carrier has denied? | May the claim be recorded as accepted? |
|---|---|---|
| day 89 | no | No — fewer than 90 days have passed |
| day 90 | no | Yes — the boundary day qualifies |
| day 120 | no | Yes |
| day 95 | yes, before day 95 | No |

## The caller's word

A caller's statement that the claim was accepted never replaces the carrier's filed position. The position recorded on the referral is the one the carrier has filed.
